evidence.summary: Vertical video (9:16) from DHS that opens on dark night-vision B-roll of an ICE raid under bold red-and-white animated captions ('Last week, ICE continued to capture criminal illegal aliens across the U.S.'), then runs a sequence of black-and-white arrestee mugshots each stamped with a red crime label (PREDATORY SEXUAL ASSAULT OF A CHILD, STALKING AND ASSAULT, SEXUAL OFFENSES AGAINST A CHILD, ATTEMPTED ARSON), with the DHS seal at the bottom. A voiceover speaks 'Leave now... we will find you, and we will deport you... America's borders are closed to lawbreakers'. There is no music track.

Open-border policies yet again have caused another preventable tragedy.

Anibal Armando Chavarria Muy, a criminal illegal alien from Guatemala, is charged with second degree murder after repeatedly stabbing a man to death in Fairfax County WITH A MACHETE.

It is common sense. ICE is calling on Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger and Virginia's sanctuary politicians to not release this murderer back into our communities.

It shows the exterior of a three-story brick apartment building behind trees and a white picket fence, then a blonde reporter in a dark blue blazer reporting outdoors near a fence, with another woman standing behind her. The lower-third reads ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED IN DEADLY STABBING, BAILEY'S CROSSROADS, VA.  [0:14] Exterior of a three-story brick apartment building behind trees and a picket fence.  [1:13] A blonde reporter reports outdoors near a fence; lower-third reads ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED IN DEADLY STABBING.  [2:11] Continued reporting with the BAILEY'S CROSSROADS, VA location banner.

transcript.text: pension. This one in Fairfax County and illegal immigrant is accused of stabbing a man multiple times with a machete in Billy's crossroads on Sunday night. Tonight, this man from Guatemala is in jail without bond. Here's our Nick Menach with more details that you'll see only on seven news. Law enforcement sources tell me that another illegal immigrant was arrested for a brutal murder in Fairfax County. The Department of Homeland Security tells seven news, Ani Bill, Armando Chavariya Muay is from Guatemala and he entered the United States illegally at an unknown place in time. This week, Fairfax County police charge Muay was second-degree murder for killing a man with a machete in Billy's crossroads. DHS has also sent an immigration detainer from Muay to Fairfax County sheriff Stacey Kincaid in order to deport him. And DHS acting assistant secretary Lauren Biss said, quote, ISIS calling on Virginia governor Abigail Spamberger and Virginia's sanctuary politicians to not release this murderer back into our communities. That in reference to the fact another illegal immigrant murder suspect in Fairfax County, Abdul Jalow, who was accused of killing Stephanie Mentor last month, was released by Fairfax County in spite of repeated warnings from police that he might kill someone. I had her for 41 years and I don't know what I'm going to do without her. Last week, Stephanie's mother called on governor Spamberger and Fairfax County officials to do more to protect Virginians from violent illegal immigrants. One of the governors, first official acts after being sworn in, was to prohibit state law enforcement from cooperating with ICE. And she has refused to answer our questions about whether she will sign a bill passed by the legislature, making it illegal for local law enforcement to do so. Nicole Kipperlove is the executive director of American Border Story, an advocacy group that works with victims of illegal immigrant crime. Immigration is not just a federal issue, but it's also a state and local issue to an extent. You see that playing out in Fairfax County. Obviously, the county has seen a lot of crime as a result of these policies. It operates under this trust policy that limits cooperation. I reached out to Sheriff Stacey Kinkade's office and I asked is her office going to honor the ICE detainers on the two murder suspects. Kinkade's office has not responded.
